newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wait over for Australian bonds as FOMC, wages loom.
newsitem.headline: Wait over for Australian bonds as FOMC, wages loom.

text.p: *Australian bonds notch up a very quiet day as the market bides its time ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting later on Tuesday and two pieces of local wages data later this week.
*Market fairly evenly split on whether Fed will lift rates.

Australian bonds ended almost flat to their previous closes after an uneventful day saw them biding their time ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting later on Tuesday and two sets of local wages data later this week.

Traders said activity had picked up in the afternoon as positions were finalised ahead of the FOMC, giving bonds a slight bid tone. A fall of the U.S. dollar against the yen, and its flow through to the Australian dollar, had little impact.
The U.S. dollar dropped over 2.5 yen to around 113 yen, and the Australian dollar lost over two yen to be near 87.50 yen late in local trade.
"U.S. bonds didn't react to it in Tokyo, that's why our market didn't react too much," one trader said. "People won't take it too hard either way until they know the (FOMC) result."

Ahead of the FOMC meeting, market opinion is fairly evenly divided as to whether the U.S. will lift rates again. Given the uncertainty surrounding the outcome, traders said it was difficult to know how the market would react to U.S. rates either remaining on hold or rising.
"The general feeling is pretty mixed about what will happen in the FOMC, so I think the market has squared up a lot of positions in the last few days," the trader said.
Past the FOMC, local markets will be faced with two sets of first quarter wages data which will also be important in shaping local rate expectations.
Data on enterprise bargaining agreements is released on Wednesday and final average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) is due on Thursday.

Recent signs of a pick up in wages growth, and comments from the Reserve Bank that wages data are a concern, have dented the confidence of those looking for a rate cut, so signs of moderate growth could see the short end strengthening while strength would basically rule one out, traders said.
Afternoon buying gives market a slight bid tone, with bonds regaining opening losses. With other markets holding basically steady ahead of the FOMC, spreads finish slightly narrower.
